input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: Order Forms auto-renew for twelve months (acceptable term length) and § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice, which meets the preferred pricing position. However, the non-renewal notice window is 180 days — more than double the 60-day fallback and beyond the 90-day walk-away threshold — so the clause fails the fallback on a material term. We propose shortening the window to 30 days and adding a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder to reach the preferred position; a window of up to 60 days would be an acceptable fallback.

ops.oldText: unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
ops.newText: unless either Party gives thirty days' advance written notice before the end of the then-current term. Vendor will notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least sixty days before the end of the then-current term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened the non-renewal notice window from 180 days to 30 days and added a 60-day renewal reminder, consistent with our playbook position that renewals must be easy to exit; a window of up to 60 days would also work for us. The 12-month renewal term and the CPI/3% uplift cap in § 8.3 are acceptable as drafted.
proposal.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice from 180 to 30 days and add Vendor renewal reminder 60 days before renewal.
